A nested lettered list restarts at (a)/(b) inside an outer paragraph also lettered (a)/(b) (e.g. s.28A(3): the outer '(a) Where any person has failed ... authorizing the Authority to-' introduces its own '(a) to discontinue...', '(b) to demolish...', '(c) to do such other acts...'). schedules.text:
1. The manner in which the land and buildings in the development area shall be used.

2. The allotment, reservation or zoning of land for different purposes.

3. The provision for regulating the uses of land and buildings in different zones such as residential, commercial, industrial and imposition of conditions and restrictions in regard to the floor area ratio, density, location, and height, number of storey and size of building and structures, the size of plots, yards and open spaces, set backs from street, building lines and the use and maintenance of buildings, structures and appurtenant land.

4. The requirements for buildings in respect of -

(a) stability of different parts of buildings foundations and super-structure;

(b) area and height, levels of floors, standards of accommodation for rooms, location and standards for staircases and exits;

(c) lighting and ventilation;

(d) fire protection;

(e) drainage of site and roof including measures necessary for rainwater harvesting; [3,36 of 2007]

(f) specifications for materials of construction and code of practice;

(g) standards and materials for plumbing and waste disposal, electrical wiring and installation such as pumps and lifts;

(h) regulations regarding clear distances of buildings from electrical, telephone, telegraph and microwave and other lines.

(i) regulations in respect of unsafe buildings and prescribing standards of fitness for buildings and other matters incidental to the ensuring of stability, safety and amenity of buildings.

5. The control of architectural features, elevation and frontage of buildings and regulations for attaining urban design objectives.

6. The provision for preserving and promoting landscaping including preservation and planting of woodlands, trees and preservation of views and prospects, places of historical, architectural interest and scenic beauty.

7. The control of pollution, environmental quality and advertisement.

8. The provision for car parking facilities, parking, loading and service bays for all types of vehicles.

9. The provisions for matters concerning and incidental to- (a) traffic and transport facilities including special facilities for pedestrians and cyclists; (b) water supply, sewerage and drainage and waste disposal facilities; (c) power supply; (d) telecommunication.

10. The provision for laying out of land for building purposes including minimum standards for access ways and roads, reservation of parks, play grounds and open spaces for other amenities and the imposition of conditions requiring the amount of land to construct or improve roads, and provide amenities or to contribute to the cost of such construction or improvement.

11. Provisions for reclamation of land.

12. The laying out and relaying out of land either vacant or already built upon, as building sites.

13. The construction, diversion, extension, alteration, improvement or closure of lanes, streets, roads and communications.

14. The construction, alteration, removal or demolition of buildings, bridges and other structures.

16. The redistribution of boundaries and the reconstitution of plots belonging to owners of property.

16. The demarcation of areas for special treatment and their detailed planning, development and redevelopment.

17. The stages by which the development plan shall be carried out.

18. The levy of fees and service charges in respect of different categories of developments.

quality_notes.issue: Section 49 refers to 'subsection (1) of section 291 (except paragraphs (a) (d) and (i) thereof) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act.' Section 40(10) drops the word 'in' from '...the amount specified in the notice appealed against...' at a line wrap, and the following bare crossheading 'APPEAL TO THE BOARD OF REVIEW' (no 'CHAPTER'/'PART' label, so the existing heading filter does not catch it) glues onto its own end. The general problem -- telling a wrapped note from a wrapped body line apart using only layout, with no reliable column-position signal in this particular document -- was not solved in the time available.

quality_notes.issue: Both sections read as scrambled prose in the source HTML itself, checked and confirmed present verbatim in the raw markup, not introduced by this parser. Section 86's footnote ('[* Section 829A is repealed by Law No. 20 of 1977]') has the same gap in isolation, with no enactment name in the footnote itself to resolve from.

SRC050.note: 144 sections, coverage 0.94% unmatched -- chapter headings (dropped, same as Part headings elsewhere) and front-matter/title-page vocabulary. quality_notes.issue: parse_consolidated_pdf.py's block-opening detection (blocks_from) only starts a new block at an enumerator when the accumulated text so far already ends in ';:.-–—' or 'or'/'and' -- the signal it uses to tell a genuine new list item from a cross-reference that happens to land beside a bracketed letter mid-sentence. The FIRST item after an intro clause that ends in ordinary words ('...the Government Agent shall cause to be prepared (a) a scheme...') doesn't satisfy that, so it stays fused into the section/subsection's own text; whichever item comes next (here, (b)) DOES split correctly, because by then the accumulated text ends in a semicolon from the fused-in first item. The same shape recurs with the SECOND item missing in section 2's 'land' definition (paragraph (a)'s raw_text swallows (b)'s content instead of the reverse) -- it is not specific to which letter, only to whichever item follows non-punctuated lead-in text. This is the same general class of gap already documented as 'inline_enumerator_not_split' for the Stamp Duty Act's section 14, here recurring at scale across a whole statute. A general fix (giving parse_consolidated_pdf.py an equivalent of build_canonical_statutes.py's split_enumerated, which scans a whole accumulated text for enumerator tokens rather than relying on line-by-line continuity signals) is real future work, not attempted here given two other general fixes in this same area regressed already-finalized statutes earlier in this session.

quality_notes.issue: The same class of gap already documented for the Land Development Ordinance and Stamp Duty Act, at unusually large scale in this statute: parse_consolidated_pdf.py's block-opening detection only starts a new list item when the accumulated text so far already ends in ';:.-–—' or 'or'/'and'. The FIRST item after an intro clause ending in ordinary words fuses into the parent's own text; whichever item follows DOES split correctly, since the fused-in first item usually ends the text in a semicolon. A programmatic scan for section/subsection text containing a mid-string ' (x) ' pattern flags roughly 65 locations across this statute -- not all necessarily genuine instances (some may be legitimate cross-references landing beside a bracketed letter), but the true count is large. Section 74's paragraph (a) and section 78's paragraph (a) were spot-checked and confirmed as genuine instances of the pattern. Not fixed here: three separate attempts at a general fix for this exact defect class, made earlier in this session while working the Land Development Ordinance and Mortgage Act, each regressed content in other already-finalized statutes and were reverted. A proper fix needs parse_consolidated_pdf.py to gain something like build_canonical_statutes.py's split_enumerated -- a full-text scan for enumerator tokens rather than a line-by-line continuity heuristic -- which is real, non-trivial future work, not attempted under this session's time constraints.

Section 36 paragraph (hh) contains its own nested (i)/(ii) sub-list ('(hh) to (i) prepare and submit... (ii) recommend to the appropriate authority...'). The first_list_item_not_split defect fuses (hh)'s own '(i)' into (hh)'s text as usual, but the resulting tree then shows FOUR children under (hh) -- 'ii', 'i', 'ii', 'ii' -- with the third and fourth carrying text that belongs to sections 36(i) and 36(j) (later paragraphs in the SAME section's own top-level list, not sub-items of (hh) at all). This is a compounding failure: once the block boundary is lost at (hh)'s own (i), the roman-numeral retyping pass (retype_roman_runs) appears to misattribute later top-level paragraph content as further (hh) sub-items. Confirmed against the source; not corrected given the same general-fix risk documented above.
